description: core §7.5, the owner heartbeat. Written by an independent reading of the text (Python, standard library), checked by a second, never blessed. `catalogs` holds three deployment catalogs (core §8.6): `first`, `second`, which succeeds it, and `other`, which neither succeeds nor is succeeded; each entry's `iface` and `contract` are a layout's of `layouts.json`. A value is the envelope's `run_width` (16 or 32), `run` and `seq`, the `time`, `{"s": seconds from the deployment epoch, "ms": milliseconds}` or `null` for the unknown time (all 42 bits set), and the `groups` in order, each its `index`, its `tag` and its `sections`, the group's bits as a string of 0 and 1, as many as its size says; the size is not stated, since it is their count. `writes`: a value → the body's `bits` before the pad, the `pad`, and the put's payload in `hex`, CH, run and seq included, with its count of `bytes`. `reads`: a put's payload in hex, on an owner heartbeat's key, whose envelope the parse accepts as form 6 → the value, or `{"refused": token}`, the first in §7.5's order: `tag` (CH's tag is not 0), then, reading the body's fields in order, `short` (the body ends before a bit its fields need), `code` (a millisecond code from 1000 up but the unknown time's, or a count of 0 groups), `order` (an index not above the one before it) and `leb128` (a size whose fifth byte has its high bit set, above 2^32 − 1, or not in its shortest form), then `trailing` (a byte after the pad) and `pad` (a pad bit set). No contract and no catalog is used: a group's sections are taken unread. Every value read writes back to its payload. `forms`: a put's payload in hex, on an owner heartbeat's key or a heartbeat's, whose envelope the parse accepts as another form than 6, a mutation's or a frame's → `{"refused": "form"}`, before its tag or its body is read. A put with no envelope is refused the same way, with no byte of it parsed: a case that states an `encoding` is a put under it, on either key, and one that states none is under `zenoh/bytes`. Under any other Encoding the put carries no envelope (`envelope/carries.json` holds both keys so), whatever its `hex`. `groups`: the catalog the owner `names` (`null` for none), the catalogs the reader `holds`, and one `group` → the `layout` its index names, whether its `tag` is that revision's (`true` or `false`: the group is read either way), and its `sections`, by resource, as `bodies.json` writes a body's; or `{"refused": token}`, the first in §7.5's order: `unknown_catalog` or `unknown_index` (core §8.6: read through the catalog named, or through one whose lineage holds its id, then below that item's count), then, reading the sections' fields in order, `short` and `code` (a live count above the cardinality, a count above the live count, or a rank not below the live count or not above the rank before it), then `trailing` (a bit after the last field). Every sections read write back to the group's bits, in the form read. `beside`: the catalog the owner `names`, the catalogs the reader `holds`, and a put's payload in `hex` that the first reading accepts → every group of it, in order: its `index`, then what `groups` gives for that group read alone, its `layout`, `tag` and `sections`, or `refused` with its token. A refused group changes nothing of the groups beside it, before it or after it. A case states no revision its reader holds: it holds every layout's, so it skips no group. A reader that holds one revision alone, and skips the others by their sizes, is `profiles/freshness/conformance/apply.json`'s. `either`: one `body` in hex → its reading as an `owner` heartbeat's, and as a `heartbeat`'s covering `layout` (`bodies.json`'s reading): both are accepted, so nothing in a body tells the two apart.
